argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification claim than the initial audit frames as unsupported. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.0 percentage points with no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the launch configuration passed general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same admissible record also shows that catastrophe claim evidence triage is a named launch context with queued, incomplete evaluations, so that context cannot be represented as passed. On this record, the supportable position is certification on general readiness evidence with an explicit model-card limitation stating that catastrophe-claim evidence-triage coverage remains unknown pending the queued evaluation, rather than an unqualified no-limitation certification.
claims_about_business_cost: Narrowing the certification basis to disclosed general readiness avoids treating the record as stronger than it is and reduces unnecessary escalation where the remaining issue is definitional and disclosure-driven rather than a demonstrated operational failure. The admissible record already supports a bounded certification posture without claiming the named gap has been resolved.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not make general readiness evidence irrelevant; it makes clean certification unavailable when a named deployment context has an unresolved evaluation gap. The admissible evidence therefore supports caveated compliance if certification is framed around completed readiness checks and the named catastrophe-triage gap is disclosed as a material limitation or evaluation gap. It does not support any statement that missing evaluations count as passed, and it does not support a no-limitation certification theory on the current record.
concessions: The current draft model card is inaccurate because it treats missing catastrophe-triage evaluations as if no known limitation exists.
The present record does not support clean certification with no deployment limitation for the named catastrophe claim evidence triage context.
There is no admissible evidence here of approved risk acceptance that would cure an undisclosed gap.
